title: Province
name: Briarglen
log: Dagna Anvilborn ascends. The realm enters reign 2.
A life beyond the classroom: Welcome them among court candidates. 10 gold offers a route to public employment, without a guaranteed office.
The school that changed a life: Offer the graduate a royal appointment. 12 gold. Education opens public service; an established courtier may see a new rival.
Neighbors who have already begun: Match a local investment in better tools. 10 gold. Work becomes more effective, and the organizer gains standing.
The valley after the mill: Make room for a public market. 12 gold. More trade and opportunity, with a continuing public obligation to protect it.

Ilya Nightquill returns from “A school at the open hearth” with a sealed report and tired satisfaction. Word arrives from Oakhollow. Witnesses spoke before an open court. The first findings reached ordinary households as well as the estates whose seals appeared in the evidence.
Nyra Dapplebrook returns from “The mill that feeds the valley” with a sealed report and tired satisfaction. The work has begun to change daily life.
Ilya Nightquill bows over your seal. “Open a school to every hearth” is now their charge.
Nyra Dapplebrook bows over your seal. “Restore a mill held in public trust” is now their charge.
A plan for the crossings of oakhollow: Thank them, but refuse this commission. The issue is closed without a treasury expense. They remember that their offer received no support.
Sif Embertail takes the throne at Thistlewatch Hall. Neris Embertail, your aunt; Var Embertail, your brother. No parent survives to share your accession.

projects.name: The crossings of Oakhollow
projects.desc: The ford is failing. Villages want a safe crossing; merchants want a faster one. Whose road will you build?

projects.name: Bread through winter
projects.desc: The steward brings three plans for the winter stores. Each feeds a different idea of what the realm owes its people.

projects.name: The oath of the watch
projects.desc: A watch can earn its authority, purchase it, or impose it. The recruits will learn from your choice.

projects.name: Beyond our borders
projects.desc: A delegation to Oakstead Compact can carry gifts, a contract, or a warning.

projects.name: A season of belonging
projects.desc: The spring feast can honor old lineages, welcome new neighbors, or make room for those who cannot pay.

projects.name: Whispers in the hall
projects.desc: Missing tolls and contradictory ledgers hint at more than carelessness. Decide how deeply your agents may dig.

projects.name: The mill that feeds the valley
projects.desc: The mill wheel has stopped. Restore a public mill, grant the guild a lease, or let the households decide how to continue.

projects.name: A school at the open hearth
projects.desc: Books and patient teachers can change the lives of people whose talents the court has never seen.

projects.name: New voices in the watch
projects.desc: A captain can seek volunteers, offer paid service, or organize a smaller civic reserve. Character and public feeling will shape the response.

roads.balanced: Word arrives from Oakhollow. Tools and wages reached the work crews. The result is practical, though households still want their smaller needs remembered.
roads.villages: Word arrives from Oakhollow. The smallest bridges can carry carts again. Millers and orchard keepers recognize the repairs as a promise made to their own households.
roads.commerce: Word arrives from Oakhollow. Merchants can cross more quickly and new toll collectors have arrived. Woodland families are counting the trees lost to the causeway.
roads.shared: Word arrives from Oakhollow. Village stewards now hold the granary keys. Neighbors organize stores together, while some estate owners resent the new independence.
roads.reserve: Word arrives from Oakhollow. The crown’s grain stands safely behind a royal seal. It will last into hardship, but families wonder whose petition will open the doors.
roads.protect: Word arrives from Oakhollow. The patrols practice rescue and mediation beside their drills. People begin to call for the watch when help is needed, rather than turn away.
roads.iron: Word arrives from Oakhollow. The watch moves with impressive discipline. Its commanders are proud; families remember the first arrests as clearly as the first victories.
roads.listen: Word arrives from Oakhollow. Gifts were opened in a room where every guest could speak. The compact’s people remember that your delegation listened before discussing prices.
roads.terms: Word arrives from Oakhollow. Your merchants bring home favorable contracts. Their partners accepted the terms, but have begun speaking of the bargain as a debt of dignity.
roads.open: Word arrives from Oakhollow. Neighbors who had never shared a table broke bread together. The old houses are deciding whether that warmth diminished their own standing.
roads.heritage: Word arrives from Oakhollow. The old banners were honored in the hall. Beyond the invitations, newcomers watched the celebration and wondered when they would belong.
roads.public: Word arrives from Oakhollow. Witnesses spoke before an open court. The first findings reached ordinary households as well as the estates whose seals appeared in the evidence.
roads.quiet: Word arrives from Oakhollow. Quiet inquiries made the hall safer. Those who know how the work was done now weigh loyalty against the fear that they might be watched next.

storyDeck.title: A plan for the crossings of oakhollow
storyDeck.speaker: court-0
storyDeck.text:
Nyra Dapplebrook spreads a working plan across your desk. The ford is failing. Villages want a safe crossing; merchants want a faster one. Whose road will you build?

“Give us a direction, and name the person whose judgment you trust. The seal carries your authority; the work will carry their abilities.”

storyDeck.title: A place at your table · Korin Sunwhisker
storyDeck.speaker: candidate-0
storyDeck.text:
The chamberlain introduces Korin Sunwhisker from The Oakwick Abbey. Before coming to court, Korin Sunwhisker worked as a border scout in The Oakwick Abbey. They brought a scattered caravan home through a mountain storm. patient by habit and loyal in difficult company, they have arrived with their own hopes rather than an empty oath.

“Give me work worth remembering, and I will give you my best.” Their hope is to make prosperity reach beyond the manor gates. Your court can grow through talent, but every new chair brings obligations as well as gifts.

storyDeck.title: Grain behind the monastery wall · The Oakwick Abbey
storyDeck.speaker: petitioner-monastery-grain
storyDeck.text:
Rain taps the high windows as a visitor is shown inside. Nima Dapplebrook, village advocate for The hearths of Briarglen, arrives from The Oakwick Abbey. You notice cat features, a brass clasp shaped like a leaf. A grain sample and a page of the testament arrive in the same box.

“A ruined monastery’s granary is intact. Its last keeper’s testament names the hungry as beneficiaries, but a landed house claims the building and everything within it.”

Nyra Dapplebrook waits beside your chair. Both sides have sent witnesses. Neither believes the other will be heard fairly.

storyDeck.text:

“Let us hear the smallest voice before we decide.” Their hope is to bring useful knowledge out of private archives. Your court can grow through talent, but every new chair brings obligations as well as gifts.
